title: PermissionFile
description: Permission file that can define a default permission, a set of permissions or a list of inlined permissions.

default.description: The default permission set for the plugin

set.description: A list of permissions sets defined

DefaultPermission.description:
The default permission set of the plugin.

Works similarly to a permission with the "default" identifier.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

PermissionSet.description: A set of direct permissions grouped together under a new name.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does.

Permission.description:
Descriptions of explicit privileges of commands.

It can enable commands to be accessible in the frontend of the application.

If the scope is defined it can be used to fine grain control the access of individual or multiple commands.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri internal convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

commands.description: Allowed or denied commands when using this permission.

scope.description: Allowed or denied scoped when using this permission.

platforms.description: Target platforms this permission applies. By default all platforms are affected by this permission.

Commands.description:
Allowed and denied commands inside a permission.

If two commands clash inside of `allow` and `deny`, it should be denied by default.

Scopes.description:
An argument for fine grained behavior control of Tauri commands.

It can be of any serde serializable type and is used to allow or prevent certain actions inside a Tauri command. The configured scope is passed to the command and will be enforced by the command implementation.

## Example

```json { "allow": [{ "path": "$HOME/**" }], "deny": [{ "path": "$HOME/secret.txt" }] } ```

allow.description: Data that defines what is allowed by the scope.

deny.description: Data that defines what is denied by the scope. This should be prioritized by validation logic.

anyOf.description: Represents a map of [`String`] keys to [`Value`]s.

oneOf.description:
The call-detail commands, for a call UI that shows more than `sew-voice:default` gives:
`call_details` (the key state and security code, the quality, every media participant with
its engine identity and label, and the ring, for a window opened mid-call), `ring` and
`ring_ended` (an incoming DM call, set from Sew's ring and cleared when it stops). Their events
(`sew-voice://security`, `roster`, `quality`, `incoming`) reach every window. Not in
`sew-voice:default`: grant it next to it, or `sew-voice:allow-call-details`,
`sew-voice:allow-ring` and `sew-voice:allow-ring-ended` one by one.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-call-details`
- `allow-ring`
- `allow-ring-ended`

oneOf.description:
Everything a call UI needs: join, leave, mute, list devices, switch devices, read the call
state and answer a recording's notice (`sew-voice:allow-join`, `allow-leave`, `allow-mute`,
`allow-devices`, `allow-set-device`, `allow-state`, `allow-consent`,
`allow-withdraw-consent`). Every window gets every event (`sew-voice://state`, `participants`,
`speaking`, `errors`, `devices`, `recording`). A window that should only watch a call can list
`sew-voice:allow-state` and `sew-voice:allow-devices` alone instead of this set.

#### This default permission set includes:

- `allow-join`
- `allow-leave`
- `allow-mute`
- `allow-devices`
- `allow-set-device`
- `allow-state`
- `allow-consent`
- `allow-withdraw-consent`

oneOf.description:
The device-key commands, for a window that signs the person out: `forget_server` (deletes the
devices of one Sew install, the hardware keys included, and answers the removed keys) and
`known_device_keys` (lists the keys the device store holds). Not in `sew-voice:default`: grant
it, or `sew-voice:allow-forget-server` / `sew-voice:allow-known-device-keys` alone, only to the
window that needs it.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-forget-server`
- `allow-known-device-keys`

oneOf.description:
The recording commands (Sew 0.9.0), for a call UI with Record and Stop buttons:
`start_recording` and `stop_recording`. Each is the person's own act, which the host's provider
sends to Sew with the person's session; Sew decides who may. Answering a recording's notice
(`consent`, `withdraw_consent`) is in `sew-voice:default` and needs nothing more. Not in
`sew-voice:default`: grant it to the call window, or `sew-voice:allow-start-recording` /
`sew-voice:allow-stop-recording` one by one.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-start-recording`
- `allow-stop-recording`

oneOf.description:
The video commands, for a window that shows or sends video: `video_caps`, `video_devices`,
`set_video_device`, `camera`, `screen_sources`, `screen`, `preview`, `video_sink`,
`video_sink_update`, `video_sink_close`, `request_keyframe`, `camera_permission` and
`request_camera_permission`, and the video codec setting `set_video_codec_preference`. The
frames reach only the window
that opened the sink (its own channel). Not in `sew-voice:default`: grant it to the call
window, or single `sew-voice:allow-<command>` permissions (a window that only shows video needs
`allow-video-sink`, `allow-video-sink-update`, `allow-video-sink-close` and
`allow-request-keyframe`). The OS asks for the camera and screen recording itself.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-video-caps`
- `allow-video-devices`
- `allow-set-video-device`
- `allow-camera`
- `allow-screen-sources`
- `allow-screen`
- `allow-preview`
- `allow-video-sink`
- `allow-video-sink-update`
- `allow-video-sink-close`
- `allow-request-keyframe`
- `allow-camera-permission`
- `allow-request-camera-permission`
- `allow-set-video-codec-preference`
